cards.claim: Spectral estimation enables reaching target accuracy with fewer Newton-Schulz iterations than fixed baseline
cards.conditions: Muon optimizer, GPT pretraining (160M-1B parameters), saved momentum matrices, target squared RMS error ε
cards.effect: Spectral estimation picks shorter routines than fixed PE, especially for MLP matrices (e.g., reaches same validation loss with δ=5-7 vs deeper fixed depths)
cards.evidence: Pretraining results (Table 4) and offline orthogonalization accuracy (Table 2)
cards.quote: With δ = 5 and δ = 7 iterations it reaches the same validation loss, so more accurate orthogonalization brings no further gain. With only five iterations, our method reaches a lower loss than the fixed baseline at any depth, so adaptation can replace extra iterations.

cards.claim: Different matrix types (attention vs MLP) require different orthogonalization depths due to different spectrum widths
cards.conditions: Muon pretraining, attention-query and MLP-up momentum matrices across layers and training time
cards.effect: Attention spectra are broader (require deeper routines), MLP spectra more concentrated (converge faster)
cards.evidence: Spectral analysis of real training matrices (Figure 3) and offline accuracy results (Figure 7)
cards.quote: Orthogonalization difficulty varies across matrix types, layers, and training time... Attention spectra are broader and MLP spectra more concentrated, and both vary across layers and training.

cards.claim: Broader spectral design intervals require more Newton-Schulz iterations to achieve fixed target accuracy
cards.conditions: Quintic polynomial iterations, design interval [λ_min, λ_max]
cards.effect: Minimax error strictly increases with interval width; achieving fixed ε eventually requires more iterations
cards.evidence: Theoretical result (Theorem 1) with proof in Section A.2
cards.quote: By Theorem 1, a broader interval gives strictly larger minimax error at every fixed depth. As ∞, the error approaches one, so achieving a fixed target accuracy eventually requires more iterations.

cards.claim: Routine selection can be reused across multiple steps rather than recomputed every step
cards.conditions: Muon or OKLS pretraining, beyond early training phase when spectra change gradually
cards.effect: Reduces computational overhead of measurement and selection, selection performed every k steps instead of every step
cards.evidence: Implementation strategy in spectral estimation method
cards.quote: Beyond early training, spectra change gradually, so we measure every k steps and reuse the selected routine in between.

cards.claim: Fixed orthogonalization depth becomes accuracy-saturating at a depth-dependent threshold
cards.conditions: Muon 160M parameter model, varying Newton-Schulz iteration depths (δ = 5, 7, 9)
cards.effect: Beyond δ=5-7 iterations, additional orthogonalization depth provides no further validation loss improvement
cards.evidence: Pretraining experiment varying depth at fixed depth (Table 4)
cards.quote: With δ = 5 and δ = 7 iterations it reaches the same validation loss, so more accurate orthogonalization brings no further gain.

cards.claim: Lower precision (bf16) measurements preserve routine selection quality for spectral estimation
cards.conditions: Spectral moment measurements in Newton-Schulz iterations, bf16 vs exact arithmetic
cards.effect: Routine selection outputs are nearly identical between exact and bf16 precision measurements
cards.evidence: Offline validation comparing measurement precision (Section F.4)
cards.quote: Offline moments are computed exactly from the saved spectra, and bf16 measurements give nearly the same selections

cards.claim: Offline spectral estimation reduces orthogonalization error at fixed Newton-Schulz depth or reduces depth for target accuracy
cards.conditions: Saved Muon momentum matrices from FineWeb run, target squared RMS error ε, fixed depth or variable depth selection
cards.effect: Substantial RMS error reduction on MLP matrices (30-40% at fixed depth); MLP matrices reach ε with 2-3 fewer iterations than fixed PE
cards.quote: With a target accuracy, spectral estimation picks shorter routines than fixed PE, especially for MLP matrices

cards.claim: Spectral estimation improves final validation loss in end-to-end LLM pretraining for multiple optimizers
cards.conditions: GPT decoder-only pretraining, 160M-1B non-embedding parameters, Nemotron-CC v2 dataset, Muon and OKLS optimizers
cards.effect: Spectral estimation matches or improves on periodic SVD-based selection and beats fixed baseline across all model sizes
cards.evidence: Pretraining results table (Table 3) and per-depth analysis (Table 4, Figure 8)
cards.quote: Spectral estimation improves on the fixed baseline for both optimizers at every model size, and it matches or improves on periodic selection from an exact SVD or eigendecomposition
